about.title: Daly City Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: Work in Daly City looks different depending on which block you're standing on. Some people spend their shifts stocking shelves along Mission Street, while others drive deliveries up John Daly Boulevard or merge onto I-280 in a company van. When a shift ends with an injury, the path forward isn't always obvious. California workers' compensation typically covers you regardless of who was at fault, and it is usually your only claim against your employer. But if someone outside your employer caused the harm — a subcontractor on a job site, a property owner who ignored a hazard, the manufacturer of a defective tool, or another driver who hit you while you were on the clock — a separate injury claim may exist alongside workers' comp. Daly City recorded 257 injury collisions in 2025, and some of those involved people who were simply doing their jobs. Our team can help you sort out which claims apply to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Daly City Workers Choose Us

items.title: We look past workers' comp
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your only remedy against your employer, but it does not cover pain and suffering. We check whether a negligent third party — a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver — opens a separate claim.

items.title: Timing and reporting matter
items.desc: California asks you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party claim generally must be filed within two years. Getting started early helps you keep both windows open.

items.title: Retaliation is illegal, and our consultation is free

items.question: I was hit by another driver on I-280 while making deliveries for my Daly City employer. Do I only have workers' comp?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Because you were working, workers' compensation should cover your medical care and part of your lost wages no matter who caused the crash. Since the other driver is a third party rather than your employer, you may also have a separate injury claim against that driver, which can include damages workers' comp doesn't pay. We can evaluate both tracks together so they don't work against each other.

items.question: Can I sue my employer directly for an injury at work in California?
items.answer: In most situations, no. Workers' compensation is the exclusive remedy against your employer regardless of fault, which means you receive benefits without proving negligence but generally give up the right to sue them. The exception is when someone other than your employer contributed to the injury — for example, a subcontractor on a shared job site or the maker of a defective machine. Those parties can be pursued separately.

items.question: How quickly do I need to report a workplace injury in Daly City?
items.answer: Tell your employer within 30 days, ideally in writing, even if the injury seems minor at first. Waiting longer can jeopardize your workers' compensation benefits. If a third party was involved, that separate claim carries a two-year deadline, but evidence like surveillance footage or a police report from San Mateo County can disappear much sooner, so acting promptly protects you.
